text:
oncall-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: GPU kernel failures > 15s (cluster: infer-eu-west-1, pool: gpu-reserve-2). Alert id: PD-987654. Auto-scaling muted.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-987654 fired (HIGH). Routed to rotation: gpu-oncall. Escalation in 5m if unacked.

jamie: acked. Looking.

jamie: quick snapshot from metrics: 90th latency jump on /v1/generate-embed, memory pressure on nodes 3/5 in pool.

priya: logs from affected pod (short):
```
I0315 14:02:10.123456 1 allocator.cu:345] cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
E0315 14:02:10.123789 1 runtime.cc:412] GPU kernel launch failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
W0315 14:02:10.124100 1 kvcache.cc:221] kv cache eviction thrashing
```

chen: nvidia-smi snapshot from node infer-eu-west-1-node-27:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.60.13    Driver Version: 525.60.13    CUDA Version: 12.0 |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr.|
| 0   A100-40G     Off           | 00000000:3B:00.0 Off | N/A             |
|    52C, 100W / 400W | 40955MiB / 40960MiB | 99% GPU util |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

chen: I see memory at near-100% and repeated kernel failures, likely fragmentation + batch size spike.

priya: any recent rollout on model variants or batcher config?

jamie: No rollout. But yesterday we enabled dynamic-batcher (experiment) for embed routes. Could be interaction.

sre-lead: Action plan: 1) temporarily throttle batcher for embed routes, 2) drain problematic pods and restart, 3) if repeat, scale up pool by +1 node, 4) start post-incident auth to check customers impacted.

priya: throttling batcher now for route /v1/embeddings (set max_batch_tokens=1024 -> 512). Command: `kubectl apply -f embed-batcher-config --namespace=inference`

oncall-bot: Change applied by priya. Batcher config updated.

jamie: draining pod infer-embed-27-57fd: `kubectl cordon infer-eu-west-1-node-27` then `kubectl delete pod infer-embed-27-57fd`

chen: pod restarted on node-31, new pod memory usage looks normal so far. nvidia-smi shows 12GB used.

pagerduty-bot: PD-987654 acknowledged by jamie. Escalation paused.

cust-success-bot: Noted — customer-facing incidents: some embed requests to acct-prod-42 reported 500s for ~2min window. I'm opening a ticket to CS.

priya: rolling logs show a pattern: periodic kvcache thrash every ~30s and then OOM. Suggest enabling kvcache cap to limit memory per-request as temporary safeguard.

jamie: applied kvcache cap for embed-worker: `KV_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=1000` and env reload.

chen: after throttles + kvcache cap, kernel failures dropped. GPU mem now 70-80% instead of 99%.

sre-lead: good. keep monitoring 10m. If stable, handoff to next oncall with notes.

jamie: current status: degraded -> stabilizing. No new PD alerts in last 4m. Latency back to pre-incident baseline for most requests, small tail remains.

priya: leaving a few follow-ups: 1) revert dynamic-batcher experiment until we analyze batching distribution, 2) add alert for kvcache eviction rate > 50/min, 3) run a memory-defrag test on model container images.

jamie: oncall handoff: I'm handing to priya for the night. Priya, can you take over monitoring for next 4h?

priya: taking handoff. Will watch metrics (gpu-mem, kvcache-evictions, embed-latency) and escalate if >3 errors in 10m.

pagerduty-bot: PD-987654 status changed: Resolved -> monitoring. (Auto message).

jamie: postmortem notes to follow, initial customer impact: brief embed 500s to ~1200 requests across 3 customers, worst impact window ~14:01-14:04 UTC, mitigated by throttle + pod restart.

cust-success-bot: Created CS ticket CS-3302 and assigned to account team for proactive outreach.

sre-lead: Nice quick run. Need owner for follow-ups: priya for batcher revert and alerting; chen for memory profiling; jamie write brief incident summary in #postmortems tomorrow.

priya: acknowledged. I'll open follow-up tasks and ping infra for optional pool scale test. emoji :white_check_mark:

jamie: closing thread for now — will update if anything flares. :hand:
